properties.name: A session with no seed node can still orient, so the moment with the most time available is not the moment the design brain is least usable
properties.statement:
A session that has not yet been given a lane, a scope or a seed node must still be able to ask what the design holds — because that is the moment it has the most time and the least to do. (Distinct from the FACT the guard named, which records the observation; this is the intent, and it gathers three adjacent costs the fact does not carry.)

⭐ THE REPORTER'S SENTENCE IS THE REQUIREMENT: "the moment with the most time available — sitting AVAILABLE, nothing to do — is the moment the design brain is LEAST USABLE, and the moment I am busiest (mid-lane) is when I am told to orient."

THE MEASURED SHAPE. Every piece of guidance says orient before you touch anything, and the orientation tools are built around a SEED: `detect_gaps` and `detect_defects` want a scope, `claim_region` wants a `seed_id`. A worker at pool check-in has no lane and therefore no seed. The only seedless calls are global rollups, which their own doctrine forbids attributing to the caller. So the honest options are (a) call nothing or (b) call an unscoped tool and hedge the number in a paragraph. THEY CHOSE (a) AND RECORDED WHY — a design brain that a willing, idle, correctly-behaving session cannot use.

THREE ADJACENT COSTS FROM THE SAME SESSIONS, all about the price of asking a first question:
(a) `get_node` RETURNS PROPERTIES AND NO EDGES, so "what does this capability connect to" needs a second call and a guess about which edge type to ask for.
(b) `describe_schema{node_type}` COSTS ~15 000 TOKENS to answer "what properties does this type have", because it inlines every wildcard edge in both directions; `required_only: true` is the compact escape and drops the edges entirely. Filed twice, on two dates.
(c) `get_skill` CARRIES NO VERSION OR HASH, so a session that read a skill at minute 0 cannot tell it was revised by minute 90. Skills are SERVED precisely so they cannot go stale relative to the binary — this is the one hole left in that argument, and their words are "it makes 'I read the skill' a checkable claim rather than a durable-sounding one."

WHAT IS OWED: a seedless orientation answer — their suggestion is a `search_design`-backed "what regions exist and how big are they", or letting `detect_gaps` take a free-text topic instead of a node id, so a session can FIND its seed rather than needing one to start.

WHY THIS RANKS LAST OF THE FIVE, stated so the ordering is not mistaken for a judgement about the report's quality: nothing here produces a FALSE statement. Every requirement above it does — a green that could not fail, a write that reported success while losing data, a defect that is not one, a name that is really a report. This one is friction on correct use, which is cheaper to carry and still worth removing.

REPORTED BY dev_storyflow's fleet, 2026-08-08, with (b) also on 2026-08-09.
